title: Litespeed’s First Trail Bike: The Pisgah
content:
The Litespeed Pisgah brings all of its titanium expertise to the trail hardtail category for the first time. Read below for all of the details on the brand’s first proper mountain bike…

Litespeed Pisgah

Litespeed debuts the Pisgah, the toughest and most capable trail hardtail it has ever created. Named for the mountain biking mecca of Pisgah National Forest near Litespeed’s home in Chattanooga, Tennessee, the original Pisgah model, which debuted in 2000, was designed with cross-country in mind. But the new Pisgah is a far cry from its predecessor.

Titanium Fabrication Expertise

Advanced titanium tube shaping and a unique rear-end design built around a Tubular Yoke increase strength and stiffness where it matters most, maximizing the Pisgah’s abilities. For the Pisgah, Litespeed introduces a new, stronger titanium tubeset, Superform X. Like all Superform tubesets, it is custom-formed and cold-worked into 3D shapes with variable wall thickness to achieve targeted flex or stiffness characteristics, while maintaining the highest levels of strength. Every tube is size-specific and fine-tuned for the perfect ride.

Litespeed’s engineers also reimagined the traditional hardtail rear-end to improve strength and the riding experience. The Pisgah sends the seat tube through a pierced ovalized Superform top tube, allowing engineers to reduce wall thickness by 30% while increasing mechanical strength at the joint. This new design resists lateral and vertical loads, even before welding.

The visual star of the show is a new Tubular Titanium Yoke, which significantly widens the seatstay stance. The seatstays taper to a point before inserting into the yoke, locking them in position before welding for maximum strength. By eliminating bends, lateral stiffness is increased without sacrificing titanium’s legendary compliance. The result is a hardtail that climbs faster and descends harder, with the high-speed precision and big-hit capabilities aggressive riders demand.

Geometry, Sizing, and Build Spec

A UDH dropout is ready for modern drivetrains, but you can upgrade the frame with Litespeed’s new sliding titanium dropouts. These sliding dropouts are designed and CNC-machined in-house for maximum strength and functionality with minimal fuss and weight. They allow riders to run a singlespeed setup or fine-tune chainstay length to taste.

A slack head angle and balanced handling deliver composure in steep technical sections, while clearance for 2.6″ tires and 150mm of fork travel mean the Pisgah is purpose-built around the terrain that asks the most of a hardtail. Climb with efficiency. Then carve corners with confidence, skip across rocks and roots, and absorb G-outs without hesitation. You can have it all. Like every Litespeed, the Pisgah is proudly handcrafted in Chattanooga, Tennessee.

The Pisgah will be offered in multiple build options, including a singlespeed with a sliding dropout, with a base build featuring Shimano XT Di2, a Fox 36 Factory Grip X 150mm fork, and an Industry Nine 1/1 Sector V2 Alloy wheelset, starting at $6,999. Customers can configure and order the Pisgah today at litespeed.com.
